sources.entry: Artalk - Comment system built in Golang, providing a lightweight and highly customizable solution for adding comments to your website. (Source Code) MIT Go/Docker

summary.one_liner: Artalk is a self-hosted, Golang-powered comment system for blogs, websites and web apps, with a lightweight framework-agnostic Vanilla JS client.
summary.what_it_does: Artalk is a comment system you host yourself, with a Go server and a client described as about 40KB and written in pure Vanilla JS. The README lists features including comment moderation with content detection and spam interception, captcha options, social login, email and push notifications, and Markdown and Latex support. It also covers comment voting, sorting, search, pinning, and nested paginated lists with infinite scroll. Admin tools include multi-site isolation, page management, page view statistics, data migration and backup, and a command line interface. The README also mentions an OpenAPI-format API document and a version check with one-click upgrade. The server is deployed with a single Docker command, and the client is added to a page with an Artalk.init call that takes an element selector, site name, server URL, and page key.
use_cases: add comments to a personal blog
self-host a comment system for a website
track page views on a blog
migrate or back up comment data
how_to_run: Integrate the client: Artalk.init({ el: '#Comments', site: 'Artalk Blog', server: '<your server URL>', pageKey: '/2018/10/02/hello-world.html' })
notable: Client is about 40KB, pure Vanilla JS and framework-agnostic
Multi-site support with site isolation and centralized management
Built-in comment moderation, captcha and spam interception
Installable as binary, via go install, or through Linux distribution package managers
caveats: The README's Docker example has a malformed ATK_SITE_URL line and missing server URL value, so the exact commands need checking against the docs
Development setup and contribution details are only linked to external documentation, not included in the README
